description:
I'm an O Level student interested in space exploration, technology, and software development. I enjoy building web applications and experimenting with AI-assisted development.

For NASA Space Apps, I'm planning to work on an interactive project exploring abandoned space equipment and the stories behind their missions.

I'm comfortable with frontend development, UI design, and working with APIs.
summary:
The Last Footprint is an interactive 3D space exploration experience that brings the stories of forgotten explorers and machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond back to life.

Through cinematic visuals, interactive 3D environments, and mission archives, users can explore historic missions, including Apollo 11, Apollo 15's Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.


Our project gives these abandoned machines a digital presence, preserving their stories, achievements, and scientific contributions. It reminds people that although their missions have ended, their impact on space exploration has not been forgotten.

Every mission leaves something behind. Every footprint tells a story.
details:
Project Details – The Last Footprint

The Last Footprint is an interactive 3D space exploration experience that brings the stories of historic spacecraft, rovers, and exploration equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars to life. Users can explore missions through cinematic animations, immersive 3D environments, and interactive mission archives. Featured missions include Apollo 11, Apollo 15's Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.

The project aims to make space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and memorable by combining education with interactive storytelling. Its creative approach transforms traditional mission information into an immersive exploration experience with realistic 3D environments, cinematic camera sequences, and interactive simulations.

Technology used: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, React Three Fiber. Custom GLSL shaders power atmospheric effects and visual post-processing, while Web Audio API handles synthesized audio and 2D Canvas powers oscilloscope and simulation displays.

Key development considerations included historical accuracy, visual quality, performance, accessibility, and user experience.
